extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal/regulatory professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary procedures
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO Order excluding a registered patent attorney from practice pursuant to the USPTO's reciprocal-discipline regulation (37 C.F.R. § 11.24), describing the grounds for exclusion, the specific rules allegedly violated, procedural notices, and post-discipline duties and remedies (reinstatement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may impose reciprocal discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting reciprocal discipline identical to the state court order had been filed; Respondent had forty (40) days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Respondent's failure to file a response led to a determination that there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (predicate for reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the exclusion is 'predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state.' The underlying state action was the March 21, 2019 Order accepting resignation from the bar and waiver of privilege to reapply in lieu of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct: USPTO Rule § 11.804(b) (analog to Conn. rule 8.4(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice explains the Grievance panel found probable cause that respondent violated rules similar to USPTO Rule § 11.804(b): 'commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a practitioner.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct: USPTO Rule § 11.804(d) (analog to Conn. rule 8.4(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice states the Grievance panel found probable cause of violations similar to USPTO Rule § 11.804(d): 'engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of scope and fee: USPTO Rule § 11.105(b) (analog to Conn. rule 1.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the practitioner communicate the scope of the representation and the basis of the rate or fee to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice ties a state-grievance finding concerning rule 1.5(b) to USPTO Rule § 11.105(b): practitioners must communicate scope and basis of fees to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of advance fees: USPTO Rule § 11.115(c) (analog to Conn. rule 1.15(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that practitioner deposit into a client trust account legal fees and expenses that have been paid in advance, to be withdrawn by the practitioner only as fees are earned or expenses incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice explains the Grievance panel's probable-cause finding corresponds to USPTO Rule § 11.115(c) and describes the trust account and withdrawal limitations for advance payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client/third-party funds and accounting: USPTO Rule § 11.115(d) (analog to Conn. rule 1.15(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that practitioner notify client or third person upon receiving funds of such client or third person, promptly deliver funds or other property of client or third person upon request, and promptly render a full accounting regarding such property upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice cites the state grievance finding and maps it to USPTO Rule § 11.115(d), emphasizing prompt notice, delivery, and accounting obligations concerning client/third-party funds or property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for discipline: 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory and regulatory authority for imposing discipline (including reciprocal discipline) before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.' Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties upon exclusion: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically requires Respondent to 'comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' (Although the full text of § 11.58 is not reproduced on the page, it signals post-discipline obligations practitioners must meet.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent remains excluded until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent shall remain excluded ... until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.' This identifies the procedural route and regulatory provision for seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (Official Gazette and § 11.59 notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to publish the provided Notice in the Official Gazette and to give notice under § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to relevant state disciplinary agencies, courts where respondent is admitted, and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative remedial actions: dissociation from Customer Numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the administrative remedy: 'The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notice and opportunity to respond (service by certified mail and 40-day response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must serve a Notice and Order (here sent by certified mail with receipt numbers) and afford the respondent forty (40) days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Background recites that a Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. given) notifying Respondent and that the Notice provided an opportunity to file within forty (40) days a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on § 11.24(d)(1). Respondent's counsel communicated he did not intend to file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for finding no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a timely response, the OED may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Analysis states: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's exclusion ... is the appropriate discipline.' This explains the consequence of nonresponse under the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the Notice of Exclusion for public dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Exclusion must include identifying information, the disciplinary finding (e.g., resignation accepted and waiver of reapplication), the rules violated and how those correspond to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, and reference to where disciplinary decisions are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order supplies the exact Notice to be published, which summarizes the state court acceptance of resignation and waiver, the findings of professional misconduct, the analogous USPTO Rules cited (with brief descriptions), and where to find disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room URL).
